steps.title: Create master for PDMS chips
steps.instruction: Design a microfluidic chip identical to Chronis et al., with a worm trap 70 µm wide, 1,200 µm long and 28 µm high; fabricate a master on a silicon wafer using a 26–32 µm layer of SU‑8‑3025 photoresist to produce a pattern for 20 individual chips.

steps.title: Mix and degas PDMS
steps.instruction: Mix Sylgard 184 PDMS components (base and curing agent) in a ratio of 1:10 in a disposable plastic cup; stir with a spatula for at least 5 min; cover the cup with a lid and place it in a desiccator for ≥30 min to remove air bubbles.

steps.title: Pour PDMS onto master
steps.instruction: Fold aluminum foil around the master to form a ‘baking mold’; draw a 3 mm line on sticky tape and place it inside the mold to set chip thickness (~3 mm); pour the PDMS mixture onto the master; cover with a lid and evacuate the assembly in a desiccator for 1 h.

steps.title: Cure PDMS
steps.instruction: Place the master with poured PDMS in an oven at 60 °C for 1 h; then allow the PDMS to harden overnight (>16 h).

steps.title: Demold and cut chips
steps.instruction: Remove the aluminum foil, gently peel the cured PDMS from the master, and cut individual chips with a razor blade (dip the blade in isopropanol for smoother cutting).

steps.title: Punch inlet/outlet holes
steps.instruction: Using a 0.75 mm diameter biopsy punch (World Precision Instruments) on a plastic surface (e.g., a Petri dish), punch six locations—four fluidic inlets, the worm trap, and the waste outlet—as indicated by red crosses; keep the chip surface dust‑free with sticky tape.

steps.title: Clean and plasma treat chips
steps.instruction: Clean chip surfaces with sticky tape; clean 22 × 22 mm cover slips with sticky tape; plasma‑clean chips and cover slips (Harrick Plasma, 29.6 W, 120 s; increase time if leaks are observed).

steps.title: Bond chips to glass slide
steps.instruction: Press the plasma‑treated chip onto a glass slide with the thumb for 10 s; then cure the bonded assembly at 80 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Batch chip production note
steps.instruction: One PDMS casting yields approximately 20 individual chips; it is practical to punch and seal chips in batches of 4 to retain backups in case a chip fails.

steps.title: Prepare M13 buffer
steps.instruction: Make M13 buffer according to the recipe in the Materials and Equipment section; autoclave for 20 min at 121 °C; store at room temperature (18–25 °C).

steps.title: Prepare levamisole solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve levamisole (Sigma Aldrich) in M13 to a final concentration of 5 mM; store long‑term at –20 °C or short‑term (up to ~2 weeks) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescein solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 5 µM fluorescein solution in M13; store at room temperature (18–25 °C).

steps.title: Prepare chemosensory stimuli
steps.instruction: Dissolve desired chemosensory compounds in M13 (examples: 0.1 % SDS, 10 mM CuSO₄, 0.5 M glycerol, 0.25 M NaCl); store at room temperature (18–25 °C).

steps.title: Sedate worms
steps.instruction: Select ~10 young adult worms; place them in a 10 µL droplet of 5 mM levamisole; cover the droplet with a small petri dish to prevent evaporation; incubate for ~15 min until the worms are fully sedated and no longer move.

steps.title: Flush chip with buffer
steps.instruction: Insert a stainless‑steel pin (0.025″ OD × 0.013″ ID, New England Small Tube Corp.) into Tygon tubing connected via a valve to a 3 mL syringe filled with M13; use this assembly to flush the microfluidic chip with M13 buffer.

steps.title: Load syringes with solutions
steps.instruction: Fill four 3 mL syringes: syringes 1 and 4 with 5 µM fluorescein, syringe 2 with the chosen chemosensory stimulus, and syringe 3 with M13; connect the syringes to a pressure controller via Tygon tubing; attach the tubing and the stainless‑steel pin to the chip’s fluidic inlets.

steps.title: Place chip under microscope
steps.instruction: Position the assembled microfluidic chip on the microscope stage.

steps.title: Load worm into trap
steps.instruction: Using the steel‑pin‑M13 syringe, gently suck up a worm head‑first so it sits at the tip of the pin; insert the pin into the chip inlet; manually apply pressure on the syringe to drive the worm tail‑first into the worm trap; continue applying pressure until the worm is correctly positioned; if the worm stalls, gently vary the flow direction by pushing and pulling the plunger.

steps.title: Secure worm and close valve
steps.instruction: Leave the syringe connected to the worm‑trap inlet and close its valve to prevent the worm from being pushed back during subsequent fluidic manipulations.
